mission: SINGLE CANARY #2 - fix exactly one independently demonstrated silent omission: "except as provided in Section 6.02". No other audit finding addressed.

reproduction.fixture: the red team's scenario S9, verbatim: "The Borrower shall not make any Investment, except as provided in Section 6.02, at any time prior to the Maturity Date." with MATERIAL items on "The Borrower shall not make any Investment," and "at any time prior to the Maturity Date." only
reproduction.responsibleFunctionAndBranch: classifyUnaccountedFragment -> the `const words = contentWords(trimmed); if (words.length === 0) return STRUCTURAL_NOISE` branch in lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-accountability/source-coverage.ts
reproduction.rootCause: contentWords() returned an EMPTY array for the fragment. Every token was in the closed class: 'except' and 'provided' were listed as subordinating connectives, 'as' and 'in' are grammar, 'Section' is a structural lead-in noun, and WORD_RE (/[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'-]*/) never matches digits so '6.02' is invisible to the counter. Zero content words meant the fragment was treated as the residue of splitting a parent unit - harmless glue - when it was in fact a cross-referenced exception.

fix.change: removed the nine subordinating connectives - provided, except, unless, including, subject, notwithstanding, however, pursuant, whereas - from FUNCTION_WORDS, and corrected the module docstring's false claim that every content word in the language is outside that set
fix.linesChanged: one entry in a Set literal, plus comments
fix.whyGeneric: It is a CATEGORY removal, not a pattern match. Nothing in the code mentions the fixture, the phrase, Section 6.02, cross-references or section numbers. Any uncovered text whose only 'content' is a word that can introduce a condition, exception, proviso or override is now accountable - 'unless X', 'subject to Y', 'notwithstanding Z', 'except for W' all behave identically. The rule enforced is the mission's: such a word is never SUFFICIENT to make uncovered text harmless.
notFixed: contentWords' blindness to digits (the section number is still invisible to the counter; it was not needed to close this canary)

afterFix.contrast: when a MATERIAL item does cover the exception, coverage is clean and normal completeness behaviour proceeds

negativeControl.note: pure connective glue with no independent semantic content remains suppressible

regressionTests: A: 'except as provided in Section 6.02' stays UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE and blocks completeness end to end
B: the connective-only fragment 'and' stays safely suppressible

corpusImpact.testDelta: +2 (the two canary regression tests); the 20 failures are 9 scenarios failing in both the Pass A and the Pass B/C suite plus the corpus-wide and rollup aggregates

corpusImpact.notPatched: None of the 11 were patched, no ground truth was changed and no suppression heuristic was added to restore the old green count. Mission §4/§7: this is a diagnostic about the trade-off.
corpusImpact.tradeoffReading: The canary is closed and the cost is 10 obviously-harmless glue fragments plus 1 judgment call. Every false gap has the same shape - a bare connective sitting between an anchored clause and its anchored complement - which suggests the durable fix is structural (attach a connective to the clause it introduces when that clause is covered) rather than lexical (put the word back in the closed class). That design decision is deliberately NOT taken here.
